resources.string: The scenario watches a Bluetooth device. Cue: needs Bluetooth access to tell what is connected — it reads only the names and addresses of your paired devices, which stay on the phone and are never sent anywhere.
Without Bluetooth access, scenarios with this kind of condition will not show. You can also allow it in the system settings.
The scenario recognizes a specific Wi-Fi network. Android treats the network name as location data, so Cue: needs location access for it — it is never sent anywhere and is not used for anything else.
Without location access Cue: cannot tell which network you are connected to, and scenarios for a specific Wi-Fi will not show. You can also allow it in the system settings.
Remembering a place reads where the phone is at the moment you tap. The place stays on the phone, only for as long as its tile — it is never sent anywhere.
Without location access Cue: cannot remember the place. You can also allow it in the system settings.
The system only reveals the Wi-Fi network name with location services turned on. Without them, scenarios for a specific Wi-Fi cannot tell that you are home.

Cue: reads your calendar for the calendar widget and for scenarios that react to events. It reads only the list of your calendars and the time, title and place of upcoming events — all of it stays on the phone and is never sent anywhere.
Without calendar access Cue: cannot tell what is in your diary — the calendar tile will stay empty. You can also allow it in the system settings.
Searching contacts needs contacts access. Cue: reads only names and phone numbers, to find a contact by name as you type in the search — they stay on the phone and are never sent anywhere.
Since Android 17 an app cannot reach the home network without this permission — including a Home Assistant at http://homeassistant.local:8123. An address on the internet does not need it.
Without local network access only the address away from home works. Pick your instance under Find my Home Assistant and no permission is needed at all.
Without contacts access the drawer can only search apps. You can also allow it in the system settings.
The scenario switches the sound or the Do Not Disturb mode. Android requires a special “Do Not Disturb access” permission for that — without it the tap action will not run.

Android hides not only notifications but also what is currently playing behind a special “Notification access” permission. It is granted in the system settings, and without it Cue: can tell neither that a notification arrived nor that a player is running. We read only what your scenarios and badges need, and we never send it anywhere.
